name: Home Addition vs Detached ADU for Multi-Generational Living in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What are the trade-offs between a full home addition and building a detached ADU in Los Angeles County for multi-generational living?
mainEntity.text: What are the trade-offs between a full home addition and building a detached ADU in Los Angeles County for multi-generational living?

acceptedAnswer.text: For multi-generational families in Los Angeles County, both full home additions and detached ADUs can work, but they solve different problems. A **home addition** (such as a new wing or second story) keeps everyone under one roof. It can create larger common spaces, shared kitchens, and accessible bedrooms. However, it often requires significant reworking of existing rooms, moving mechanical systems, and reinforcing foundations and structure. Construction can be disruptive since it affects the main living areas. A **detached ADU** offers more independence, with its own entrance, kitchen, and bathroom. This can be better for adult children, aging parents, or future rental income. Detached ADUs must comply with specific zoning rules on size, setbacks, height, parking, and utility connections. Site layout, privacy, and access paths become critical, and separate sound isolation is usually easier than in an attached addition. Financially, ADUs may generate **future rental income** and can sometimes be financed or valued differently by lenders and appraisers, while additions primarily increase the main home’s size. In both cases, it is smart to compare total project costs, expected appraisal impacts, privacy needs, and local ADU ordinances before deciding which option fits your property and long-term plans.
acceptedAnswer.description: A full home addition integrates space into the main house but can disrupt existing layouts and require major structural and mechanical changes. A detached ADU adds a separate dwelling with its own kitchen and bath, offering privacy and rental potential, but needs separate utilities, access, and strict zoning compliance.
